parsed.main_gap: The subset-sum gap bound (11) does not follow from the stated averaging argument; endpoint gaps must also be handled.

errors.description: There are only 2^{n+1}-3 interior consecutive gaps, so their sum being less than 1 yields a gap below 1/(2^{n+1}-3), not d. Repair: include 0 and 1; their two gaps equal min a_i. If this is at most d, use that interval; otherwise an interior gap is at most d.
errors.quote:
They lie in $(0,1)$, so their $2^{n+1}-3$ consecutive gaps sum to less than $1$. When put in nondecreasing order, two consecutive subset sums therefore differ by at most
\[
\frac1{2^{n+1}-1}=d.
\]

parsed.notes: The claimed answer and both main constructions are otherwise correct. The sole gap is central but repaired by a short endpoint case distinction, with the remainder of the proof unchanged.
